claim: Controlled mutation separates a proposed edit from its effects. Supported operations resolve targets against current state and pass selected guards before mutation. Per-operation results include refusals; successful session operations and remediation-pass mutations use distinct attribution channels. A comparison affects admission only when its consumer refuses the prohibited edit; any direct write path lies outside this boundary.
topology: A flexible producer emits a typed proposal. The resolver uses the document structure model of current artifact state. A before-value comparison reports mismatches by default; it is not the hard admission gate. Within the controlled application boundary, the supported operation vocabulary and selected guards determine whether the applier may mutate the resolved target. Per-operation results include refusal and failure. Successful session edits and remediation-pass mutations produce distinct attribution records. Unmigrated direct edits remain outside this route.
bw_encoding: Rectangles identify models and artifacts; rounded boxes identify mechanisms, and diamonds mark admission decisions. Gray identifies flexible reasoning only. Heavy outlines mark consequential application/admission boundaries. Solid arrows carry data, models or results; dashed arrows carry verification/challenge or subordinate selection relations.
redesign: Author-approved diagnostic-evidence label distinguishes advisory before-value comparison from selected admission guards; target-resolution width adjusts to give the edge label room.
